verdict.rationale: New Relic's official CLI records APM deployment markers, and the CLI is documented as fitting into CI/CD pipelines. That is first-party release tracking, but the evidence never shows those markers overlaid on performance data to correlate them with regressions. Missing for 10: evidence that deploy markers are correlated with or overlaid on regressions in charts or incidents, tracking of configuration (non-deploy) changes, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can correlate regressions with deploys and configuration changes via release or change tracking

citations.quote: Deployment Markers: Easily record an APM Application deployment within New Relic.
You can use the New Relic CLI to manage entity tags, define workloads, record deployment markers, and much more.
Be it fetching data from your laptop while troubleshooting an issue, or adding New Relic into your CI/CD pipeline.
